I farm 12 mu, and I do not start from zero each year. I start from what worked before, then I adjust a little. Around Quzhou, wheat and maize are the steady crops, and cotton is the crop I keep for cash, but cotton takes more watching and more sprays. My family has some people working off-farm, so I cannot put all 12 mu into the crop that needs the most hand work. This year I will keep 4 mu in cotton and 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. That way I spread risk. If cotton price is not good, I still have grain. If grain price is flat, cotton can still bring cash. I have well irrigation, so I will feed the crops enough and not let them suffer for water. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than let the crop go hungry, because once yield is lost I cannot get it back. I usually look at what the better farmers nearby do, and I stay close to that, maybe a little careful on cost. For wheat I will push base fertilizer and keep 3 irrigations if weather stays normal. For maize after wheat, I will keep it simple and fast, mostly no-tillage so I save time. For cotton, I will use improved seed, enough nitrogen and potash, and I will spray more times because insects and weeds can turn that crop bad very quickly.
